system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** Based on the supplied extracts only; the underlying SPA and DD documents have not been reviewed. Figures below are proposed negotiating positions, not agreed terms. The baseline remains **AUD 24 million, debt-free/cash-free, for 100% of Paperbark**, governed by NSW law.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | A materially higher general cap, with separate treatment for fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter at 50% / AUD 12m**, subject to diligence and available recourse; 20% leaves substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Each claim must exceed **AUD 25,000**; only aggregate losses above a **AUD 250,000 deductible basket** recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket and aggregation of related claims; thresholds confined to general warranties. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, recovering all qualifying losses once crossed; the Seller’s combination materially erodes recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | General warranties: **18 months**; limitations presumptively apply to all Claims. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, separate category periods and properly notified claims surviving expiry. | **Counter at 24 months and reject universal application**; Buyer needs sufficient operating and reporting cycles to identify claims. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Separate fundamental warranties covering capacity, ownership, full capitalisation and unencumbered transfer; no basket/de minimis; materially longer survival. | **Seek a 100% purchase-price cap and seven-year contractual notification period**, appropriately documented under NSW law; ownership risk should not receive ordinary business-warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims, with no express fraud exception supplied. | An express fraud/fraudulent concealment carve-out from caps, thresholds, time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy restrictions; preserve non-excludable rights. | **Reject the blanket wording and insert an overriding carve-out**, addressing whose fraud is attributable to Seller; Seller must not contractually shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only fair disclosure with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the issue, mapped to relevant warranties; a fixed, archived disclosure record. | **Reject deemed disclosure of everything**; identify permitted specific exceptions and ensure disclosure does not qualify specific indemnities unless expressly agreed, because document availability is not meaningful risk disclosure. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room/public records. | No constructive or imputed knowledge bar; preferably no knowledge exclusion, otherwise narrowly defined actual knowledge of named Buyer personnel. | **Delete “discoverable” and adviser-imputation wording**; diligence access should not transfer unidentified warranty risks to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied merely by delivering written consent. No final consent or evidence of condition satisfaction supplied. | A binding consent covering the transaction, with clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, no unacceptable adverse amendments and effectiveness at Completion. | **Make effective consent and satisfaction of its conditions a Buyer-waivable completion condition**, with a long-stop/termination right; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout figure, repayment through completion funds flow and effective release of all relevant security, guarantees and change-control exposure at Completion. | **Require an agreed lender payout/release mechanism at Completion, with prompt registration discharge undertakings**; Buyer should not acquire a secured target while paying on a debt-free basis. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses are “for Seller”, but omitted from funds flow; on-costs unresolved. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, including amounts payable after Completion. | **Expressly allocate and quantify these amounts in the price mechanics/funds flow, backed by a specific indemnity**; omission otherwise leaves Buyer funding Seller’s transaction costs, with no double counting. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, with no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective transfer of all relevant IP rights, plus protection against ownership, infringement and business-disruption consequences of the identified defect. | **Require payment evidence and confirmatory assignment at/before Completion; broaden the specific indemnity beyond the fee**; settling an invoice alone may not cure chain-of-title risk. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational issue, considered immaterial; access, scope and notification requirements remain unresolved. | Prompt evidence-based investigation, containment, preservation of evidence, legal assessment and any required notifications/remediation; tailored financial protection. | **Require investigation deliverables, pre-completion covenants and a specific indemnity, with security if warranted**; uncertainty does not justify either dismissing the issue or asserting a confirmed notifiable breach. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals are ordinary-course operating costs. | Review the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, scope, cancellation rights, accruals and departure from ordinary course. | **Reserve classification pending DD; require Buyer approval for material new commitments and appropriate pricing treatment if warranted**; neither “ordinary course” nor debt-like treatment follows automatically from the figures. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance extend across all Claims. | Express, internally consistent regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, specific indemnities, payment/price obligations, covenants and fraud. | **Replace the all-Claims sweep with a category matrix and express precedence rules**; otherwise general boilerplate can defeat separately negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Seller holding 100%. | Independent reconciliation of issued capital and ownership, certificates/issuance and transfer records, constitution and shareholder rights; checks for security, options, convertibles and competing interests. | **Verify rather than accept the register alone, and require completion transfers, releases and updated registration**; registered ownership is not conclusive evidence of an unencumbered, fully diluted 100% acquisition. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP are said to be settled under the general regime. | Separate pre-completion tax protection with appropriate exclusions and claims control; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement warranties, with tailored limits and survival. | **Mark both expressly open**: seek tax survival of at least seven years and longer where assessment remains possible, and negotiate IP-specific protection outside the 18-month/20% default; Seller’s assertion does not establish Buyer agreement. |

**Priority:** Do not accept the package globally. Resolve Bluefen, Riverlark, bonus funding and Ironquay completion protections, while expressly reserving the liability architecture and unresolved incident, tax and IP terms.
=== END ADVICE ===
